title: Daily capture histories of 70 marked Rhionaeschna caligo, rainy season, high Andes of Colombia, 2024
creator: Arango Quintero, Sebastian; Bota-Sierra, Cornelio Andres
citation: Arango Quintero, S., & Bota-Sierra, C. A. (2026). Capture histories of the dragonfly Rhionaeschna caligo Bota-Sierra, 2014 (Odonata: Aeshnidae) [Dataset]. figshare. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31120483.v1
abstract: Capture-mark-recapture of Rhionaeschna caligo, an odonate endemic to the high mountains of the Colombian Central and Occidental Cordillera, Andes, sampled daily in two seasons of 2024 (April and June-July) for Cormack-Jolly-Seber survival estimation. This table is the rainy season file (18 sampling days).
samplingProtocol: Daily capture, marking and recapture of adult odonates over a sampling season (days of effective sampling); sex, wing length and (for the damselfly) age class and mite load recorded at marking.
closureNote: Each sampling day is a period (CJS over days). The other season is a separate table with unlinked individuals.
geographicCoverage: High mountains of the Colombian Central and Occidental Cordillera, Andes (no site or coordinates deposited)
covariateNote: unit_sex: male or female. unit_wing_mm: wing length (mm). unit_wing_class: the source's wing-length class (big, medium, small).

notShipped.dates: the calendar dates of the sampling days are not deposited

notes: Teneral individuals have rows from the day they were marked; adults and juveniles from day 1 (E4.4). The item description gives 18 days for April and 22 for June-July; the deposited files are labelled dry season (22 days) and rainy season (18 days).
